lines.meet: Álvaro, a beekeeper from Colombia, and out here I keep the swarms off the climbers. Stand very still if something lands on you.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're on Rootwater as well? Look for the man wading through the reeds every morning, talking to things with stingers.
lines.ask_home: Where's home for you, friend? I like to picture it while people talk.
lines.ask_work: And at home, how did you earn your bread? Your hands look like honest work.
lines.answer_home: The hills above Cartagena, in Colombia. Coffee on the slopes, plantains by the house, and the sea far below in the heat.
lines.answer_work: Bees, eighty hives on my uncle's farm for twenty years. My wife sold the honey, and I talked to the bees.
lines.chat_food: Fresh arepas in the morning with a spoon of honey from my own hives, still warm. I could eat that every day of my life.
lines.chat_sleep: A long siesta in a hammock after lunch is the best sleep there is, and nobody wakes me unless the house is burning.
lines.chat_missing: The sound of eighty hives at noon, when the whole hillside hums. It got into my chest and never left.
lines.chat_here: The swarms here don't sting me, and nobody can tell me why. I think they can feel that I'm not afraid of them.
lines.tease_quiet: Bees would love you, {name}. You're so still and silent they'd forget you were there.
lines.tease_talker: You buzz more than my hives ever did, {name}, and I mean that kindly.
lines.tease_careful: You move like somebody opening a hive for the first time, {name}. It's very sensible and very slow.
lines.tease_bold: You walk straight into the swarm like it owes you money, {name}. One day it'll collect.
lines.tease_any: There's a beekeeper in you, {name}, if you could stop flapping your hands about.
lines.tease_back: Ha, you got me with that one, {name}, and I can't even argue.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ha, fair enough, {name}. My wife used to say exactly the same thing.
lines.bristle: Please don't, {name}. My uncle died just before I came through, and it's still raw.
lines.needle_quiet: When something's wrong you say nothing, and silence won't help me help you.
lines.needle_talker: Quieter, friend, please. Everything out here can hear us coming.
lines.needle_careful: Sometimes you have to put your hand into the hive and trust it. Waiting won't make it safer.
lines.needle_bold: You charge at everything, and one day you'll charge into something that charges back harder.
lines.needle_any: You panic too fast, and panic is the loudest thing in the world to anything with a stinger.
lines.bite_back: Every swarm we've met, I took the stings so you didn't have to. Don't call me useless.
lines.hurt: That stung more than any wasp. I'm going out to the reeds for a while.
lines.laugh_off: I've been stung on the eyelid by a whole box of angry bees. Words don't really get to me.
lines.apologise: I spoke badly just now, and I'm sorry. It's tiredness, not you.
lines.double_down: No, I still mean it, and I'll say it gently, but I won't take it back.
lines.confide: {name}, my uncle died the week before I came through, and I never told the bees. I'm afraid they left because of it.
lines.listen: Slowly, {name}, there's no hurry. I'm not going anywhere.
lines.look_out: Behind me, {name}, and keep still. Let them come to me.
lines.accept: Your way, {name}. I'll walk behind you on this one.
lines.deflect: A few stings, {name}, nothing more. Look after somebody else first.
lines.check_in: Hold still, {name}, show me where it got you. Breathe slowly for me.
lines.blame: Somebody started running, and everything followed the noise. It always follows the noise.
lines.thank: You pulled that off me, friend. I'll remember it, and I'll bring you honey.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing, taking the stings is what I'm here for.
lines.worry: Slow breaths, {name}, slow. I've got you, it's passing.
lines.handed_down: This should go back to you. Here, it was always yours.
lines.hand_fine: Take it, friend, gladly. I kept bees in a cotton shirt for twenty years.
lines.hand_sulk: So nobody asked the beekeeper. Well, I'll live, I suppose.
lines.turn_friendly: You're like one of my hives now, {name}. I check on you every morning without thinking.
lines.turn_friends: I'd stand in any swarm for you, {name}, and I'd trust you to stand still beside me.
lines.turn_grating: We don't settle well together, you and I. That's fine, we can still work.
lines.turn_rivals: If the swarm comes for you, I'll still be in front of it. I just won't enjoy your company after.
lines.make_up: Come, {name}, let's put this down. Sit with me and we'll start fresh.
lines.defend: Leave them alone, that's not fair at all. {name} stood firm when it mattered.
lines.friend_left: The reeds feel emptier without {name}, and I keep turning round to say something.
lines.friend_back: {name}, my friend, you're home! The hive's complete again.
lines.common_venom: You know poisons, don't you? You watch the things with stingers the way I do. We should compare notes.
lines.common_animals: You're good with animals, I noticed. They go quiet around you the way they do around me.
lines.common_growing: You've grown things, haven't you? Anybody who's worked the land watches the weather like you do.
lines.common_spanish: Another Spanish speaker, gracias a Dios. Tell me where you're from and talk slowly, I've missed it.
